g.text: How a team task moves from a Switch room message to verified completion
RULE: A task is completed only after Saarathi verifies the PR and its checks. AI can understand a request, but it
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN SOMEONE SUBMITS A PR?
helper sends a PR link to
Task owner or room lead starts work.
Task owner or room lead records why work is waiting.
Task owner or room lead confirms the blocker is fixed.
Only the verifier can do this after proof passes.
An authorized person submits a PR link.
Every proof rule passes and the save succeeds.
GitHub is unavailable, a check is missing/running, or
the task changed. Task stays open.
A permanent rule fails. Task stays open until
• PR is in an approved repository.
• PR author is the task owner or an explicitly listed
• Every changed file fits the task’s allowed file
patterns. Renames check old and new names; deletions
• Every required check passed on the exact commit
• Missing or running checks never count as a pass.
• For reruns, use the latest start time; for Actions,
the highest run attempt. A newer pending run overrides
Saarathi stores the result for each
message. A replay returns that same result
and cannot complete the task twice.
Leave the task open and retry after a
webhook, scheduled check, or backoff delay.
A newly running check cancels an older
Before saving, compare task and policy
versions. If either changed, save nothing;
Replies are queued durably. A worker claim
expires after a crash. A lost
acknowledgement may cause a duplicate reply;
Completing a prerequisite sends a “ready” notice. It does not silently change another
task. The dependent task stays Blocked until its owner or team lead resumes it.
WHAT WE SAVE FOR A TRUSTWORTHY RECORD
Task store is the source of truth. The audit log only grows. The proof record stores the
exact commit SHA and check IDs. Inbox records track received and processed messages
separately. SQLite is used for the demo; the storage interface can move to Postgres.
Terms: SHA = exact commit identifier. Version check = confirm task and rules did not change during GitHub review. File patterns use case-sensitive,
Known limit: a push can arrive after GitHub’s final read but before the database save. The saved proof stays tied to the exact commit that was checked.
